Why go: the Gulf's best dive sites in a day from Samui

Koh Samui's own reefs are shallow and modest. The famous diving in this part of the Gulf is at Sail Rock, a granite pinnacle rising from deep water between Koh Phangan and Koh Tao with a vertical swim-through called the Chimney, and around Koh Tao, including Chumphon Pinnacle, a seamount whose top sits at about 12 m. This fast catamaran makes both possible as a day trip, with two dives or two snorkel sessions, lunch on board and a dive platform that makes getting in and out easy.

Snorkellers come along on the same boat, so mixed groups of divers and non-divers can travel together.

Who it suits, and who should choose something else

  • Good for: certified divers staying on Samui who don't want to move to Koh Tao, and snorkellers who want clearer water than Samui's beaches.
  • Choose something else if you want to learn: a course is better done over several days. See our diving guide.
  • Snorkelling only? The Koh Tao and Koh Nang Yuan day trip adds the famous sandbar and viewpoint.

Good to know

  • Season: visibility at Sail Rock is best from March to September. November and December bring swell and murkier water.
  • Whale sharks: they are seen at Sail Rock some years, mostly in spring, but never guaranteed.
  • Safety: dive within your certification and experience; Chumphon Pinnacle has currents. Rent a computer if you don't own one.
  • Seasickness: the open-water crossing can be lively. Take tablets an hour before departure.

Planning your dives

If you have only one dive day, Sail Rock is the single most rewarding site; book the Koh Tao or Chumphon days if you have already dived Sail Rock or want two different sites. Snorkellers see most at Koh Tao's sheltered bays. Dive within your training and depth limits, and carry dive insurance that covers hyperbaric treatment.
